supersedes: M2P3_FREEZE_V1.json for every author session that starts after this freeze is merged; V1 stays the record for package A
why_v2: Under V1 the frozen static guard rejected package A (STAGE2.md, ledger row 59). The guard's stated rule is correct; its implementation was not: the regex forbade any open() with a literal-string path in a write mode, so it rejected the spec-mandated write when spelled literally, and accepted a write to any path held in a variable. V2 corrects the implementation only.

what_changes.static_guard: guard_v2.py (sha256 prefix d7b3c480c7cfb7c0): permits exactly one open() in a write mode whose target resolves to worlds.jsonl (a string literal, or a module-level name bound once to that literal) and forbids every other open(); V1's forbidden modules and all other forbidden calls are unchanged
what_changes.orchestrator: m2p3_check_v2.py (sha256 prefix 1b8c5c5c07dccbce): the M2-P2 orchestrator m2p2_check.py with static_guard delegating to guard_v2 and nothing else changed (verified: 17 changed lines against main's m2p2_check.py, the docstring line and the body of static_guard only)
what_changes.rule: UNCHANGED: no filesystem access beyond the one required write; no network, environment reads, threads or subprocesses

what_does_not_change: the neutral spec (sha256 6a25c7f3…), the author unit (claude-haiku-4-5, fresh session, identical wrapper), the taxonomy hostile and token list, the determinism rule, the floors, compilation, the viability floor, G-SURF, the arms, the statistics, the 50 % effect-size primary, the 80 % terminal and the co-registered −88 % ± 8 point prediction: all exactly as M2P3_FREEZE_V1.json

calibration.guard: guard_v2_calibration.log (sha256 prefix b65d6781e8d8ebc3; script guard_v2_calib.py 96df535ec2652412), expectations fixed in the script before the run: CALIBRATION PASS 8 cases. The real M2-P2 emitter ACCEPT and package A's emitter ACCEPT (its write is legitimate); six tamper controls REJECT (a second write, a write to another path, M2-P2's filename variable rebound to '../worlds.jsonl', an extra read, an os.environ read, a subprocess import). V1's pattern accepted the rebound-variable tamper, a false negative, and rejected package A, a false positive.
